sections.title: Overview
descriptions: Gregory Hazard’s complaints concern two encounters with AFPD Officer Zachary P. Goodale. Outside a building Hazard owned, a woman initially parked to eat in the shade, telling responding officers she had not realized it was private property. After Hazard asked her to leave and photographed her license plate, she moved her vehicle to the office entrance, blocking access. She told officers she had moved there to knock on his door and remained because she wanted to discuss the photograph. Hazard called AFPD. Goodale later arrived, disparaged Hazard to the woman, and said he would “traumatize him for you.”

In a separate encounter on April 19, 2024, Hazard questioned Goodale about parking in an accessible parking space at the police department. During their exchange in the north parking lot, Goodale told Hazard that returning would result in a trespassing charge and recorded that he had trespassed Hazard from the lot. The department’s subsequent findings and apologies for both encounters are summarized in the Department Response tab.

sections.title: Department Response
descriptions: Hazard’s June 9, 2026 City Council handout includes Chief Cameron Paul’s findings on both complaints. Hazard supplied the handout; the chief’s letters within it are department-authored records.

Office-entrance incident — In his May 15, 2025 letter (COM-2025-010; case 24AF02000), Paul found that Goodale violated department policies, including conduct unbecoming an officer. He cited Goodale’s disparaging remarks about Hazard and his statement that he would traumatize him. Paul also found that Goodale had not obtained Hazard’s account or reviewed available surveillance video, leaving the investigation short of the department’s expectations for objectivity and completeness.

Accessible-parking incident — In his May 13, 2025 letter (COM-2025-009), Paul found violations of department policy and state law, including unlawful parking in an accessible space. He rejected Goodale’s assertion that he was allowed to park there and said Goodale should not have issued Hazard a trespass order and lacked authority to do so. A separate letter identifying the April 19, 2024 encounter (case 24AF03376) rescinded the order and confirmed that no related trespass order remained.

Paul apologized on behalf of the department and city in both findings letters. He said Goodale’s January 2025 resignation prevented him from imposing discipline, but that both complaints and his findings would be retained in department records.
